title: From the American Revolution to the 20th century

atoms.b:
The Boston Tea Party
In the late 18th century, tensions were on the rise between the ((American_colonies)) and the British Empire. The Empire had spent a lot of money on the Seven Year's War (1756-1763), which it was trying to gain back by introducing new ((taxes)) for the colonies.

hint.text: The Seven Year's War was fought between multiple European nations on multiple continents. Land disputes between Great Britain, France and Spain in North America were only one of many areas of conflict.
hint.label: Seven Year's War

atoms.b:
The colonists felt this was unfair, since they were not even represented in the British ((parliament)) and were therefore not involved in the decision, leading to the slogan: “No taxation without ((representation)).”
In 1773, American colonists threw ((tea_imports)) into the Boston ((harbor)) to protest against these taxes. This event became known as the ((Boston_Tea_Party)).

atoms.b:
The American Revolution
The 13 American colonies fought for their independence from ((British_rule)) in the ((American_Revolutionary_War)) (1775-1783). One year into the war, five of the Founding Fathers wrote the ((Declaration_of_Independence)), which was officially approved on July 4, 1776.

After their victory, ((George_Washington)), who had led the Revolutionary War, was elected first ((president)) of the United States of America in 1789.
The Bill of Rights, which consists of the first ten constitutional ((amendments)) and guarantees certain rights for US citizens, was adopted in 1791.

atoms.b:
The 19th and early 20th century
The United States continued their ((colonization)) westward during the 19th century, resulting in the deaths and displacement of many ((Native_Americans)).
The settlers believed they had a right to “manifest destiny” by claiming the ((land)) and resources for themselves.

Even the tribes that were considered “civilized”, meaning those that had partially ((adapted)) to American settler culture, were still not considered ((equal)) to White settlers. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 called for the “Five Civilized Tribes” (Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Muscogee and Seminoles) to be forcibly ((relocated)) into a territory set aside for them to live in while the ((settlers)) claimed their original homeland. Many died on the long and ((exhausting)) way. This act of ethnic cleansing became known as the Trail of Tears (1830-1850).

The early 20th century
The 18th and 19th amendment were passed in 1920. The former banned the sale and production of alcohol, while the latter granted women the right to ((vote)). The so-called Prohibition of alcohol was an attempt to fight alcohol-related issues, but also gave rise to organized crime profiting off ((illegal_sales)). The 18th amendment was ultimately repealed in 1933.

atoms.b:
In 1924, the Indian Citizenship Act acknowledged Native Americans as US ((citizens)). However, it took until 1957 for all states to allow them to vote as well.

The Wall Street stock market crash of 1929 led to a period marked by ((poverty)) and unemployment known as the ((Great_Depression)) (1929-1939). It affected not only the US ((economy)), but other states around the world as well, especially Germany and the UK.
